name: Fawn Color
lede: Fawn is the light brown of a young deer's coat, a name that sits in Ridgway's 1886 nomenclature and in a 1535 list of pleasing color pairs.

sections.title: A color of the coat
sections.body:
Paterson glosses the camel's coat as *the fawn colour*, equal to beige [1]. In 1535 Fulvio Pellegrini Morato named grey with fawn among the most beautiful combinations, by the account of Pastoureau [2][3].

Our library carries the name in Ridgway's 1886 nomenclature, again in his 1912 standards (plate XL) and in the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 [4]. Measured against the ISCC-NBS categories, the swatch is nearest to light brown, 3.1 units of ΔE2000 away [4]. Its neighbors are [[fawn]], [[camel]], [[beige]] and [[buff]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This tone appears in 968 paintings in our archive, 4.07 per cent, as photographed [5]. It is twice as common in Mughal paintings as elsewhere, in 17 of 168 [5]. Frans Hals has it in 7 of 23 [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [5].

openers: Fawn and grey were called a beautiful pair as early as 1535, long before photographs of paintings.
